reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Jurisdiction: Wisconsin
    Focus year: 2021
    Question: Is the county sheriff's office an entity empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?
*/

% ----------------------------
% Basic domain vocabulary
% ----------------------------

state(wisconsin).

focus_year(2021).

% Treat "writ of eviction" as the Wisconsin "writ of restitution" used in eviction actions.
writ_kind(writ_of_eviction).
writ_kind(writ_of_restitution).

writ_synonym(writ_of_eviction, writ_of_restitution).
writ_synonym(writ_of_restitution, writ_of_restitution).

% Entity classification for reasoning.
entity(county_sheriffs_office).
entity(county_sheriff).
entity_role(county_sheriffs_office, sheriff).  % common-sense mapping for "sheriff's office" -> sheriff
entity_role(county_sheriff, sheriff).

% ----------------------------
% Statute translation: WI Stat  799.44 (2021)
% ----------------------------

/* WI Stat  799.44(1) (2021) - Order for judgment in eviction actions.
   If the court finds plaintiff entitled to possession, it must immediately enter an order
   for judgment for restitution of the premises.
*/
statute_79944_1_must_enter_judgment_for_restitution(State, Year, EvictionAction) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    EvictionAction = eviction_action,
    court_finds_plaintiff_entitled_to_possession(EvictionAction).

/* WI Stat  799.44(2) (2021) - Writ of restitution issued; may be delivered to sheriff for execution.
   Also: "No writ shall be executed if received by the sheriff more than 30 days after its issuance."
*/
statute_79944_2_court_must_order_writ_issued(State, Year, EvictionAction) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    EvictionAction = eviction_action,
    statute_79944_1_must_enter_judgment_for_restitution(State, Year, EvictionAction).

statute_79944_2_writ_may_be_delivered_to_sheriff_for_execution(State, Year, Writ) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    writ_synonym(Writ, writ_of_restitution).

statute_79944_2_no_execution_if_received_more_than_30_days_after_issuance(State, Year, IssuanceDay, ReceiptDay) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    integer(IssuanceDay),
    integer(ReceiptDay),
    ReceiptDay - IssuanceDay > 30.

% If receipt is within 30 days, this statute does not bar execution (it does not itself compel execution).
statute_79944_2_execution_not_barred_by_30_day_rule(State, Year, IssuanceDay, ReceiptDay) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    integer(IssuanceDay),
    integer(ReceiptDay),
    ReceiptDay - IssuanceDay =< 30.

/* WI Stat  799.44(3) (2021) - Stay of writ of restitution up to 30 days upon hardship,
   conditioned on payments; may require bond; if default, writ may be issued forthwith.
*/
statute_79944_3_court_may_stay_issuance_up_to_30_days_if_hardship(State, Year, StayDays) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    integer(StayDays),
    StayDays >= 0,
    StayDays =< 30.

statute_79944_3_stay_conditions_include_payments(State, Year) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021.

statute_79944_3_court_may_require_bond_as_condition(State, Year) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021.

statute_79944_3_if_defendant_defaults_then_writ_may_be_issued_forthwith(State, Year) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021.

/* WI Stat  799.44(4) (2021) - Writ directed to sheriff of county where property located;
   contains command to remove defendant and restore possession; return within 10 days.
*/
statute_79944_4_writ_directed_to_sheriff_of_county_where_property_located(State, Year, County) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    atom(County).

statute_79944_4_writ_commands_sheriff_to_remove_defendant_and_restore_plaintiff(State, Year) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021.

statute_79944_4_writ_return_within_10_days(State, Year, ReturnDays) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    integer(ReturnDays),
    ReturnDays =< 10,
    ReturnDays >= 0.

% ----------------------------
% Legal conclusion rule: empowerment to execute a writ of eviction (restitution)
% ----------------------------

/* An entity is empowered by WI Stat  799.44 (2021) to execute a writ of eviction (restitution)
   if the writ may be delivered to the sheriff for execution and the entity is (or acts as) the sheriff.
*/
legal_entity_empowered_to_execute_writ_of_eviction(Entity, State, Year) :-
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    entity(Entity),
    entity_role(Entity, sheriff),
    statute_79944_2_writ_may_be_delivered_to_sheriff_for_execution(State, Year, writ_of_eviction),
    statute_79944_4_writ_commands_sheriff_to_remove_defendant_and_restore_plaintiff(State, Year).

% ----------------------------
% Scenario (facts from the question)
% ----------------------------

% The question asks about a county sheriff's office and its power to execute a writ of eviction.
scenario_state(wisconsin).
scenario_year(2021).
scenario_entity(county_sheriffs_office).
scenario_writ(writ_of_eviction).

/* Scenario statement succeeds when the encoded scenario facts are all present. */
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_state(State),
    scenario_year(Year),
    scenario_entity(Entity),
    scenario_writ(Writ),
    State = wisconsin,
    Year = 2021,
    Entity = county_sheriffs_office,
    Writ = writ_of_eviction.

% Provide one minimal eviction-action finding fact to complete the statutory context.
% (Not strictly required for empowerment, but included to reflect 799.44's eviction-action setting.)
court_finds_plaintiff_entitled_to_possession(eviction_action).

% ----------------------------
% Answer
% ----------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    scenario_state(State),
    scenario_year(Year),
    scenario_entity(Entity),
    legal_entity_empowered_to_execute_writ_of_eviction(Entity, State, Year),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    !.

% ----------------------------
% Main entrypoint (required)
% ----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Is the county sheriff’s office an entity empowered by law to execute a writ of eviction?
